Prompt to build this component

When to use it

When to use

  • To switch between two to four views of the same thing: Desktop and Phone, Grid and List, Default and Error.
  • To pick one of two to four short, mutually exclusive options where seeing all of them at once helps: Blank or With example, Day, Week or Month.

When not to use

  • For five or more options, or long labels: use cmp-select.
  • For moving between separate pages: use links or the navigation composites.
  • For independent on and off choices: use cmp-checkbox.
  • For actions: use cmp-button.
Variants, anatomy, accessibility, interaction and content rules

Variants

  • default — a compact track that is as wide as its options; for toolbars, page headers and filters. The base class alone; no modifier class.
  • fill — the options share the full width equally; for narrow screens, panels and forms.

Anatomy

  • Root: <div class="ds-segmented-control" role="radiogroup" aria-label="<what it switches>">; add ds-segmented-control--fill to fill the width.
  • Option: <label class="ds-segmented-control__option"> holding the input and the option's words, and optionally an icon before the words.
  • Input: <input class="ds-segmented-control__input" type="radio" name="<group>" value="<value>">, one checked. It covers the option invisibly, so the whole option is the target.
  • The selected option is drawn as a raised segment on the track; nothing else marks it.

Accessibility

  • Built on native radio buttons: Tab moves into the group to the selected option, the arrow keys move and select, and the choice is announced with its position ("Phone, 2 of 2").
  • The group has an accessible name (aria-label, or aria-labelledby pointing to a visible heading).
  • Every option has words: beside its icon, or, for an icon-only option, in a ds-visually-hidden span.
  • Each group's name is unique on the page. In a screen with several states, give each state's copy its own name (view-default, view-error) so one does not uncheck the other.
  • The selected segment differs by fill, edge and weight, never by colour alone.

Interaction

  • Hover darkens the option's words and selection moves the raised segment, both within the quick duration; nothing changes size (int-01, int-03).
  • Focus shows the shared ring around the focused option and stays there after choosing (int-02).
  • Switching a view updates the content in place, without moving the control (int-05).

Content rules

  • Options are one or two words in sentence case, parallel in form: "Desktop", "Phone"; "Blank", "With example".
  • Order options by frequency or natural sequence, and select the most common one by default.

Do and don't

  • Do keep the control next to the content it switches.
  • Do keep the same options in the same order every time the control appears.
  • Don't mix icons and words across options; give every option an icon, or none.
  • Don't use a segmented control to submit a form or trigger an action.
